candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; coordinate discharge planning, referrals, client education, and continuity of care during transitions
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — DSMES referral during transition to a new insulin regimen
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize that DSMES is an ongoing process and should be reassessed and provided at critical times such as diagnosis, unmet goals, new complicating factors, and major transitions in treatment or care.

options.A: A new referral for diabetes self-management education and support is appropriate because major treatment and care transitions are critical times to reassess education and support needs.
options.B: Repeat DSMES is unnecessary because evidence-based diabetes education is intended to occur only once at diagnosis.
options.C: DSMES should be repeated only if the client specifically requests printed educational materials.
options.D: A new insulin regimen does not change self-management needs, so prior education should be considered permanently sufficient.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care recommend DSMES at diagnosis, annually and/or when treatment goals are not being met, when complicating factors develop, and when transitions in life and care occur. A hospital discharge with a new insulin regimen represents a meaningful treatment and care transition that can change self-management skills and support needs. B and D incorrectly treat education as a one-time event. C is too narrow because DSMES is an interactive, person-centered process that includes problem-solving and behavior support rather than only printed information or client-initiated requests.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current ADA standards treat DSMES as ongoing support that should be revisited at defined critical times, including major treatment and care transitions rather than only at initial diagnosis.
candidate.source_document_title: Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being to Improve Health Outcomes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
candidate.source_locator: DSMES Recommendation 5.2 and accompanying text — provide DSMES at diagnosis, annually and/or when not meeting treatment goals, when complicating factors develop, and when transitions in life and care occur; DSMES is an ongoing person-centered process
candidate.source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
candidate.stem: A client with type 2 diabetes completed diabetes self-management education several years ago. The client is now being discharged after a hospitalization with a new insulin regimen and says, “I already had diabetes education when I was diagnosed.” Which nursing response is best?
